scope: Independent STATIC bounded ordinary library QA against SPEC0209; packet only

findings.title: Document row identities bypass cell redaction and copy literal bodies
findings.evidence: extractDocument constructs key from raw context()/columns[0], passes it as the symbol, and emitFor stores symbol verbatim. projectJsonContract only redacts the shape cells. Heading text is also copied into context without classification.
findings.static_counterexample: A declared persistence-catalog table whose first data cell is function guest() { return 1; /* DOC_BODY_MARKER */ } copies that body into entry.symbol even though the corresponding shape cell becomes UNKNOWN. A code-bearing heading has the same path.
findings.impact: Generated catalog still copies guest implementation text through document metadata. UNKNOWN shape classification does not remove leaked symbol bytes.

test_gap.detail: Existing other-channel test puts the body in the second cell and uses safe headings/first cell, so it does not cover the identity path.

findings.remediation: Classify all document-derived identity text; use a stable opaque digest for unsafe row/heading/anchor components, retain owner/source/UNKNOWN metadata and requirement entries, and check absence across the entire serialized catalog.

findings.title: TypeScript literal property/member names still copy implementation strings
findings.evidence: nodeName returns string-literal node.text without the filtering used by staticData or printed. Object initializer property names go straight into shape.properties[].name; interface/class literal names go straight into the serialized symbol.
findings.static_counterexample: export const Options: Record<string, boolean> = {"function guest(){return 1;/* TS_NAME_BODY_MARKER */}": true}; The body is copied into the property name. An interface method with that quoted name similarly copies it into the member symbol.
findings.impact: The no-implementation-copy boundary can be bypassed through a literal key inside an otherwise static initializer or declaration. Protecting literal values/types alone is insufficient.

test_gap.detail: Tests cover executable AST nodes, initializer values and schema defaults/examples, but not string-literal keys/member names.

findings.remediation: Apply bounded name projection to string-literal keys/member/module/export names too. Preserve unsafe names as UNKNOWN hash/length metadata and use stable digest-based identities rather than raw source text.

findings.title: Python bytes annotation literals bypass opaque literal projection
findings.evidence: Python typ permits every ast.Constant, but only inspects constant values that are str before ast.unparse. A bytes constant therefore reaches unparse unchanged and is returned as annotation/base text.
findings.static_counterexample:
def run(value: b'function guest() { return 1; /* PY_BYTES_BODY_MARKER */ }') -> int:
    pass
findings.impact: Literal guest implementation bytes are copied into Python annotation metadata. With ordinary parameter/return annotations this path also has no UNKNOWN marker for that literal.

test_gap.detail: Tests cover lambda expressions and str annotation literals/__all__, not bytes annotation literals.

findings.remediation: Handle bytes constants explicitly as opaque hash/byte-length UNKNOWN values, or reject all non-vocabulary literal kinds before unparse; retain the declaration, owner and source provenance.
